summary: Describes how to use PPP over SONET and SDH circuits, the fiber-optic transmission systems used by carriers. It is a standards-track proposal. It was replaced by RFC 2615.

plainLanguage.summary: A way to carry PPP over very fast fiber links. A newer version replaced it.

questions: how to use ppp on fiber
subtitle: Running PPP over fiber-optic SONET and SDH circuits.

tldr.problem: PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) was designed for leased lines and modems, but carriers have high-speed SONET and SDH fiber-optic links that need the same simple encapsulation.
tldr.mechanism: PPP frames are mapped directly into SONET/SDH Synchronous Payload Envelopes. The octet stream is aligned with SPE boundaries, with no scrambling needed, and a standard signal label indicates PPP content.
tldr.outcome: Carriers can use the lightweight PPP encapsulation over fiber links, achieving higher throughput than other SONET/SDH payload mappings and simpler line termination equipment.

today: RFC 1619 defined PPP over SONET/SDH as a standards-track proposal. It was later replaced by RFC 2615.

sections.title: PPP over Fiber-Optic Lines
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) is a standard for transmitting multi-protocol data over point-to-point links. Originally deployed on dial-up modems and leased phone lines, PPP works equally well over high-speed fiber circuits. SONET (Synchronous Optical Network) and SDH (Synchronous Digital Hierarchy) are fiber-based transmission standards used by telephone carriers, with transmission rates from 51.840 Mbps up to 2.488 gigabits per second.

This RFC describes how to run PPP directly over SONET and SDH circuits, allowing carriers to use PPP's simple encapsulation for private point-to-point fiber links. The lightweight overhead of PPP enables higher throughput than alternative SONET payload mappings.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP is a simple protocol designed for point-to-point links. SONET and SDH are fiber-optic circuits that carriers use. This RFC shows how to put one inside the other.

sections.title: Physical Layer Mapping
sections.content:
PPP presents an octet-oriented synchronous interface to the physical layer. The octet stream is mapped into the SONET/SDH Synchronous Payload Envelope (SPE), with octet boundaries aligned to SPE boundaries. No scrambling is applied during insertion.

The Path Signal Label (C2 byte) is set to the experimental value 207 (hex cf) to indicate PPP content. The basic transmission rate is STS-3c/STM-1 at 155.520 Mbps, providing 149.760 Mbps of available information bandwidth. Lower rates use SONET/SDH Virtual Tributary mechanisms to map existing signals asynchronously or with byte-synchronous methods.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP data gets put directly into the fiber's payload space, like packing boxes into a truck. The label on the truck says it contains PPP.

sections.title: Framing and Configuration
sections.content:
The framing for PPP over octet-synchronous links uses HDLC framing. PPP frames are variable in length and can cross SPE boundaries, allowing efficient use of the link. Configuration uses standard LCP (Link Control Protocol) defaults, with recommended options including Magic Number, 32-bit frame check sequence (FCS), and no address/control or protocol field compression.

PPP does not require control signals from the physical layer. When available, such signals can improve functionality and performance.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP breaks data into variable-length frames that can wrap around the fiber payload boundaries. The setup is simple and uses the standard PPP defaults.
